pointers.sentence: `django.utils.numberformat.format` writes a number with the separators and grouping it is given; `django.utils.dateformat`, through `DateFormat` and `TimeFormat`, writes a date or a time by a format string of letters, with the names of months and days from `django/utils/dates.py`; and `django.utils.timesince.timesince` and `timeuntil` put the time between two datetimes into words.

`django.utils.numberformat.format` takes the number, the decimal separator and, optionally, the places after the point, the grouping and the thousands separator (`django/utils/numberformat.py:format`).
A grouping may be a sequence, the size of each group in turn leftwards from the point: `(3, 2, 0)` is Indian English's, as `NUMBER_GROUPING`'s documentation says (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).
A caller that wants rounding rounds first, as the `floatformat` filter does, half up ([The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)) (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:floatformat`).

`Formatter.format` splits it with `re_formatchars`, the letters that have a meaning and no backslash before them; it calls the method for each letter and makes its result a string, and copies the text between, dropping each escaping backslash (`django/utils/dateformat.py:Formatter.format`).
`TimeFormat` has the letters of a time of day and four of the zone's, `"e"`, `"O"`, `"T"` and `"Z"`; `DateFormat` subclasses it and adds the rest (`django/utils/dateformat.py:DateFormat`).

The zone's letters need a zone, and `TimeFormat.__init__` gives the formatter a zone only for a datetime: an aware value's own, or for a naive one the default time zone, `TIME_ZONE` (`django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.__init__`).

`django/utils/dates.py` holds the words the letters write, as dictionaries of lazy translations made at import: the days of the week, and the months in four sets, `django.utils.dates.MONTHS` for `"F"`, `MONTHS_3` for `"b"` and, title-cased, `"M"`, `MONTHS_AP` for `"N"` and `MONTHS_ALT` for `"E"`.
The comment on `MONTHS_ALT` says only that some locales require it for a long date (`django/utils/dates.py:MONTHS_ALT`).

"a.m.", "p.m.", "midnight" and "noon" are messages `TimeFormat` translates as it writes them: in German, `"P"` writes the first arrival, made local, as "11:30 vorm." (`django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.P`, `django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.a`). The suffix `"S"` writes is English in every language: "29th".

(`django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.P`, `django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.a`). The suffix `"S"` writes is English in every language: "29th".
`django.utils.timesince.timesince` gives the time from one datetime to a later one in years, months, weeks, days, hours and minutes, ignoring seconds (`django/utils/timesince.py:timesince`).
`timeuntil` is the same with the two exchanged (`django/utils/timesince.py:timeuntil`).
`avoid_wrapping` makes each part's spaces non-breaking (`django/utils/html.py:avoid_wrapping`), and the parts are joined by `", "`, itself a message: Arabic's catalogue has "، ".
